To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following problems are polynomial time solvable: - The red-blue set cover problem with a red set containing a single element, - The red-blue covering by disjoint sets problem with a red element, - The minimum red-blue set cover and red-blue covering by sets problem with the consecutive ones property for all red and blue sets, - The minimum covering by disjoint sets and the minimum red-blue covering by set problem with the consecutive one property for all blue and red sets.

(a) the red-blue covering problem is polynomial time solvable for the consecutive ones property, (b) the problem remains NP-hard if we restrict the input sets to have at most two non-zero entries, and (c) the problem is also NP-hard for the consecutive ones matrix property.
the consecutive ones property is a powerful tool for making red-blue covering problems polynomially solvable, but it is also a powerful tool for showing hardness results.
